PPE Violation Detection

AI-driven PPE detection systems utilize computer vision and deep learning algorithms to monitor workers in real-time through existing CCTV infrastructure. These systems identify whether individuals are wearing mandatory safety gear such as helmets, vests, gloves, and goggles. Upon detecting non-compliance, immediate alerts are sent to supervisors, enabling prompt corrective actions and reducing the risk of workplace injuries

AI-powered ANPR systems use standard or specialized CCTV cameras (often IR‑enabled) to detect, read, and log vehicle registration plates in real time through deep learning and OCR-based computer vision pipelines.
These systems typically follow a multi-stage process:
Image capture using high-resolution or infrared cameras to ensure clarity under varied lighting or speed.
Plate localization identifying potential plate regions via contrast and shape, followed by filtering algorithms to refine detection.
OCR or AI-based recognition converts plate images into text using deep neural nets trained on diverse fonts, languages, and environmental conditions.

Data processing & integration matches the extracted plate data against databases (e.g. stolen vehicles or authorized access lists) to trigger actions like alerts, access control, or automatic challan issuance
Automatic Number Plate Recognition

AI-enhanced fire and smoke detection transforms standard CCTV cameras into early warning systems, capable of identifying flames or plumes of smoke in real‑time through visual anomalies, flame movement patterns, or pixel‑area thresholds.

These systems can operate on existing ONVIF cameras—and often at the edge—eliminating the need for expensive sensors or cloud processing, minimizing latency and enabling on-site alerting for faster response.

By monitoring subtle cues before conventional detectors trigger, they significantly reduce response times and false alarms, sending instant alerts via mobile, VMS, or alarms to help prevent escalation and damage.
Fire & Smoke Detection

AI-based video analytics track and measure vehicle speed directly from CCTV feeds by detecting each vehicle, following its movement across frames, and calculating speed using calibrated pixel-to-distance mapping or dual line zone crossings.
Accuracy and enforcement-grade versions use high-precision radar paired with cameras to capture real-time speed, license plate, vehicle type, and time data, even in low-light or adverse weather.

Automated alerts and integration with traffic management systems enable immediate notification of violations, real-time enforcement dashboards, and analytics on speeding patterns for proactive traffic safety interventions.
Speed Detection
AI-powered object detection and counting systems analyze live video feeds from cameras to detect, classify, and count products or items on shelves, conveyor belts, or in packaging lines in real time.
These modules combine deep-learning models to identify individual items and track their movement across frames, allowing accurate counts even when items overlap or move quickly.
The solution can be deployed edge‑based or cloud‑based for seamless reporting, dashboards, and analytics
Product Counting

AI‑based video analytics utilize camera feeds (often installed overhead or at entry points) to detect and count individuals—typically by identifying human heads or full bodies—while tracking movement across frames efficiently.
Core process:
Detection via deep learning models to locate each person in frame
Tracking to follow movement across frames
Counting using virtual lines or zones for entries/exits
Filtering to prevent double‑counting and manage occlusion using tracking and calibration algorithms
Head/People Counting

The system performs face detection on video frames, isolating facial regions from background elements. Then it maps key landmark points (eyes, nose, jawline, etc.) and converts them into a unique numerical template or faceprint that is matched against stored identities.
Face Recognition

Using AI-powered cameras or proximity sensors, these systems detect obstacles — including humans, visible object and fixed infrastructure — as a forklift moves. Once a threat enters a defined safety zone, an immediate audible beep or alarm is triggered to alert the operator.
Forklift Automation

Vision-based, contactless monitoring: Uses standard camera video streams to continuously monitor zones (e.g. hallways, patient rooms, living areas). No wearables required—individuals can move freely without carrying devices.

AI-driven detection of falls: Combines pose estimation, posture analysis, optical flow, and fall classification to detect sudden vertical-to-horizontal motion or prone positions. Algorithms flag likely fall events and avoid false alarms from normal movement.
Real-time alerts & seamless integration: Generates immediate notifications—via SMS, mobile app, VMS alerts, or dashboards—to caregivers or staff.
Fall Detection

AI-based PIDS monitors defined perimeter boundaries (e.g., fences, walls, virtual zones) via CCTV cameras and intelligent video analytics to detect unauthorized entries by humans or vehicles in real time. It transforms passive CCTV into proactive, defense-grade surveillance.
Perimeter Intrusion Detection

Our AI-driven system is designed to identify and respond to movements of large animals in sensitive areas like highways, industrial zones, and forest boundaries. By analyzing live camera feeds, it provides instant alerts, reduces the risk of accidents, and ensures safety for both people and wildlife. This solution not only protects human lives but also contributes to conservation efforts by preventing harmful encounters.
